cases.purpose: Append to existing differently permissioned files, then copy, move and remove each using ordinary tools.
cases.oracle: The original bashsyslogd deferral and documented interface, RFC syslog PRI facility numbers, Linux Unix/UDP datagram and file-link semantics, and the explicit fixture vectors. The independent Python sender and loopback receivers supply exact bytes; timestamp and hostname prefixes are checked as a bounded format using the guest hostname, not matched against candidate-derived expectations.
cases.comparison: The VM-only observer owns its Unix and loopback sockets and daemon. Setup proves Unix empty/nonempty queue ordering, line matcher positive and negative controls, hardlink and symlink behavior, and for config the IPv4/IPv6 loopback and FIFO reader/writer handshake. A SIGHUP reload is synchronized by an observed config FIFO reader before each probe. Original files, bounded raw stdout/stderr, datagrams, process status, comparison details and socket state are captured in the case tree and HOME diagnostic JSONL. Each case compares exact records and explicit normalized results; mismatch or timeout remains failure. Before copy/move/remove, the diagnostic JSONL retains each pathname, expected permission bits, raw initial and final st_mode, and device/inode values, allowing independent per-file mode review.
cases.stdout: lifecycle appended=yes modes=yes copied-moved-removed=yes stopped=yes socket-removed=yes stderr-empty=yes
